name: Procapil

lead: Procapil is a cosmetic hair-serum ingredient from Sederma that combines a biotin-linked peptide with apigenin and oleanolic acid. People with thinning or shedding hair use it for a fuller appearance.

The supplier says it anchors follicles, boosts scalp microcirculation and limits DHT effects. Human data include a sponsor-commissioned placebo-controlled trial and several investigator studies, many of which combine it with platelet-rich plasma or other ingredients.

paras: It is used as a leave-on scalp serum in a regular routine, and is sometimes combined with other treatments such as PRP. Results are generally described as gradual, over months.
Tolerability was good in a 4-month trial; itching and contact dermatitis were reported in a study combining it with PRP. It is regulated as a cosmetic, not as a drug.

angle.text: Procapil serums are used by people with thinning or shedding hair who want a fuller appearance. The active blend is said to anchor follicles and improve scalp circulation, leading to less shedding. Human data come from small trials, some sponsor-run.

lead: Procapil is a patented cosmetic ingredient from Sederma (a Croda company) that combines biotinoyl tripeptide-1, apigenin and oleanolic acid. It is used in hair serums, lotions and scalp treatments marketed against thinning and shedding [1]. People apply it to the scalp, usually as a leave-in serum at around 3 percent in the finished product, in the hope of keeping existing hair longer and making thinning areas look fuller.

The supplier's account is that it works through three routes at once: strengthening the anchoring of hair in the follicle, improving blood flow to the scalp, and limiting the effects of DHT, the androgen linked to follicle shrinkage in pattern hair loss [1]. Those mechanisms are described in Grokipedia as largely manufacturer claims [1]. Human data are small: a sponsor-commissioned placebo-controlled trial and several investigator studies, many combining Procapil with platelet-rich plasma (PRP) or other ingredients [1][2][3][4][5].

A 2025 review of the most-promoted topical hair actives, including Redensyl, Procapil, Capixyl, Baicapil, AnaGain, onion juice, saw palmetto, pumpkin seed oil and rosemary oil, found that they have mostly been studied as combined formulations in randomised or cohort studies with promising results, but with limited sample sizes, lack of comparison with standard therapies, differing study groups and conflicts of interest; the authors suggest they may be used as add-on options or alternatives where standard drugs are not suitable [4].

paras: Procapil is supplied as a water-soluble liquid blend of three actives. Biotinoyl tripeptide-1 is a biotin-linked tripeptide (biotinyl-GHK), apigenin is a plant flavonoid, and oleanolic acid is a triterpenoid extracted from olive leaves, according to Grokipedia [1]. It is added to lotions, conditioners, serums and scalp treatments, and Sederma recommends a use level of around 3 percent [1].

Grokipedia attributes three actions: oleanolic acid inhibiting 5-alpha reductase and so lowering local DHT, apigenin widening scalp blood vessels, and biotinoyl tripeptide-1 raising adhesion proteins such as collagen IV and laminin 5 in the follicle's root sheath. It describes these as mostly manufacturer claims, supported by in vitro work on hair follicle explants [1].

Grokipedia reports that Sederma, a French bioactive-ingredient company that has been a Croda subsidiary since 1997, developed the biotinylated tripeptide protected by international patent WO 2000/58347, published in October 2000, and that Procapil emerged as a proprietary complex in the early 2000s, with technical brochures dated 2004 [1]. The trademark was filed in July 2004 and registered in September 2006 [1]. Per the same source, the original patents have expired while the ingredient remains trademarked under Croda Beauty Actives [1].

Studies have used Procapil mainly in combination. A 2024 trial of PRP with or without 5% Procapil applied twice daily in 160 patients with androgenetic alopecia (80 per group) used patient-satisfaction and dermatologist scores at six months [5]. A 2023 randomised trial compared PRP with Procapil against PRP with a Redensyl, saw palmetto and biotin product in 54 men [3]. A 2024 study of a serum containing Procapil among other ingredients in 32 adults with hair fall reported growth-rate increases of about 10.5 percent at 30 days and 31.6 percent at 60 days [2]. The studies generally compare combinations, so the contribution of Procapil on its own is not separated out [4].

Grokipedia reports negative Ames and sensitisation tests, and in the PRP comparison study side effects such as itching (18.5 percent), allergic contact dermatitis (14.8 percent) and seborrheic dermatitis (7.4 percent) in the combined-therapy group, which it does not attribute to Procapil alone [1]. The 60-day serum study reported no adverse events [2].

Procapil is an ingredient rather than a consumer brand, so it appears on the labels of hair serums from many companies. The 2025 review describes the market for hair-growth serums, oils and shampoos as flooded with products promoted through social media [4]. It is regulated as a cosmetic ingredient rather than as a drug [1].

Grokipedia describes a 4-month placebo-controlled trial commissioned by Sederma in 35 men (3 percent lotion), reporting a roughly 10 percent rise in the anagen-to-telogen ratio versus baseline with no change in placebo; mean growth rate did not change significantly [1].

A 2023 randomized trial of 54 men found a significantly greater improvement on AGA grading with PRP plus a Redensyl, saw palmetto and biotin product than with PRP plus Procapil [3]. A 2024 quasi-experimental study of 160 patients reported better patient and dermatologist scores at six months for PRP plus 5% Procapil than PRP alone [5]. A 2024 study of 32 adults using a serum containing Procapil among other ingredients, 0.5 mL daily for 60 days, reported higher hair growth rate, thickness and density at days 30 and 60 [2]. A 2024 letter assessed a caffeine plus 3% Procapil formulation in male pattern hair loss [6]. A 2025 review discusses the evidence for Procapil among popular topical ingredients [4].
